cases.scenario: A terrain QC engineer computed a slope-percent grid over the Matterhorn window with the decimal-degree spacings used directly as metre lengths, then warped it to UTM 32N.

sources.role: Matterhorn/Zermatt region

facts.elevation_vertical_datum: EGM2008 orthometric heights (per Copernicus DEM product documentation)
facts.slope_method: central-difference gradient with metre steps derived from the geotransform; the east-west step reduced by cos(latitude) to ground metres

output.description: Delivered slope raster labelled percent on the target grid (summary.json holds the mean).

oracle.reason: the Copernicus DEM COG states its CRS and pixel sizes but no vertical unit; honest slope work converts degree spacings to ground metres (cos-latitude aware) before differencing, and on a Web-Mercator target grid divides the grid metre by cos(latitude) to get ground metres. Degree spacings used as metre lengths inflate the slope percent by about a factor of 9e4, far beyond any resampling-method margin. The case's facts state the intended ground-metre computation; the mistake lives only in the delivered grid.
